endpoints.purpose: Encode one SVG document into geometric token IDs (L1 primitive by default; L2 composite / L3 spatial optional). The core endpoint. Deterministic given tokenizer_version + config.
endpoints.request: {"svg": "<svg viewBox='0 0 24 24'><path d='M4 4 L20 4 L20 20 Z'/><circle cx='12' cy='12' r='6'/></svg>", "level": "L1", "config": {"canvas_size": 300, "max_coord_level": 6}, "return": ["token_ids", "tokens", "metadata"]}  // level in {L1,L2,L3}; config optional (server defaults are pinned per tokenizer_version); 'return' selects payload verbosity; svg max 256KB
endpoints.response: {"tokenizer_version": "geomtok-1.0.0", "vocab_id": "geom-5561-v1", "level": "L1", "token_ids": [2,17,140,140,17,820,140,...,3], "tokens": ["<BOS>","MOVE_TO","X@140","Y@140",...,"<EOS>"], "n_commands": 4, "n_tokens": 41, "compression_ratio": 3.54, "normalization": {"viewBox_applied": true, "transforms_flattened": 1}, "warnings": []}  // tokens[] omitted unless requested; n_tokens_bpe optionally echoed for compression baselines

endpoints.purpose: Decode token IDs back into a valid SVG document (round-trip). Coordinate-faithful reconstruction; emits well-formed SVG.
endpoints.request: {"token_ids": [2,17,140,140,17,820,140,...,3], "tokenizer_version": "geomtok-1.0.0", "vocab_id": "geom-5561-v1", "level": "L1", "output": "document"}  // tokenizer_version REQUIRED for correct decode table; output in {document,element_list}; vocab_id must match the encode vocab
endpoints.response: {"svg": "<svg viewBox=\"0 0 300 300\"><path d=\"M140 140 ...Z\"/><circle cx=\"150\" cy=\"150\" r=\"75\"/></svg>", "n_tokens": 41, "valid": true, "fidelity": {"coord_mean_px": 1.78, "coord_max_px": 3.37, "canvas": 300}}  // 'valid' is FSA-grammar guaranteed for model-generated streams; fidelity returned when token stream carried reference coords

endpoints.purpose: Run the GeomTok-Eval render-based intrinsic protocol over a set of SVG scenes for a caller-supplied or built-in tokenizer. Game-resistant: scores reconstruction fidelity + render SSIM + token economy, not a gameable proxy.
endpoints.request: {"scenes": [{"name": "home_icon", "svg": "<svg ...>"}, {"name": "gear", "svg": "<svg ...>"}], "tokenizer": {"builtin": "geomtok-1.0.0/L1"}, "metrics": ["attr_err", "count_acc", "render_ssim", "token_economy"], "baseline": "cl100k_bpe"}  // 'tokenizer' is either {builtin: id} or {remote: {tokenize_url, detokenize_url}} to evaluate a third-party tokenizer through the same harness

endpoints.purpose: Synchronous batched tokenize/detokenize for up to N items in one round-trip (server coalesces into vectorized CPU work). Primary high-throughput path for vendors indexing icon libraries.
endpoints.request: {"op": "tokenize", "level": "L1", "items": [{"id": "ic_001", "svg": "<svg.../>"}, {"id": "ic_002", "svg": "<svg.../>"}], "config": {"canvas_size": 300}, "on_error": "skip"}  // op in {tokenize,detokenize}; items <= 1000 per call, total payload <= 32MB; on_error in {skip,fail_fast}

endpoints.purpose: Asynchronous large-corpus job (10k-1M icons): accept a manifest or inline+R2/S3 reference, return a job handle, process via queue, write results to caller bucket or fetchable artifact. For full-library backfills that exceed sync limits.
endpoints.response: {"job_id": "job_8f3a...", "status": "queued", "accepted_items": 240000, "poll": "/v1/batch/jobs/job_8f3a...", "created_at": "2026-06-12T00:00:00Z"}  // GET /v1/batch/jobs/{job_id} -> {status: queued|running|succeeded|failed|partial, progress: {done, total}, sink, errors_url}

endpoints.purpose: NDJSON streaming tokenize over an open connection for pipeline ingestion: client writes one SVG-per-line, server streams back one token result per line as each completes. Bounded memory on both ends; backpressure-aware.
endpoints.request: Content-Type: application/x-ndjson; transfer chunked. Each line: {"id":"ic_001","svg":"<svg.../>"}  newline-delimited. Query: ?op=tokenize&level=L1&canvas_size=300
endpoints.response: application/x-ndjson stream, one result line per input line, order-preserving: {"id":"ic_001","ok":true,"token_ids":[...],"n_tokens":41}\n{"id":"ic_002","ok":false,"error":{"code":"PARSE_ERROR"}}\n ... trailing {"_stream":"end","n_ok":N,"n_failed":M}

endpoints.purpose: Fetch the immutable vocabulary manifest (token id -> symbol table, level layout, coord grid params) so clients can decode/encode offline and pin to an exact vocab. Backs determinism + reproducibility.
List available pinned tokenizer_versions + their vocab_ids, default level, lifecycle status (active/deprecated/sunset date). Lets clients pin and migrate deliberately.
Liveness + readiness for autoscaler/LB. readyz confirms the pinned vocab tables and parser are loaded; gates traffic during cold start.

sdk:
TWO OSS SDKs wrapping the same wire API + an in-process (no-network) mode, since the tokenizer is pure-CPU deterministic and small.

PYTHON (pip install geomtok) — dual mode, one import:
  import geomtok
  # In-process (OSS, zero network): runs the Apache-2.0 library locally
  tok = geomtok.Tokenizer(level="L1", canvas_size=300)        # wraps PrimitiveTokenizer/Composite/Spatial
  ids = tok.encode(svg_str)                                   # svg -> List[int]   (mirrors tokenize_fn)
  svg = tok.decode(ids)                                       # List[int] -> svg   (mirrors detokenize_fn, Detokenizer)
  res = tok.encode_detailed(svg_str)                          # -> TokenizationResult(token_ids, tokens, n_tokens, compression_ratio, metadata)
  # Hosted (managed tier): identical surface, just point at the endpoint
  tok = geomtok.Tokenizer(level="L1", api_key="gk_live_...", base_url="https://api.geomtok.dev")
  ids = tok.encode(svg_str)                                   # same call -> POST /v1/tokenize transparently
  out = tok.encode_batch([svg1, svg2, ...])                   # -> POST /v1/batch, auto-chunks to <=1000, retries idempotently
  for r in tok.stream(svg_iter): ...                          # generator over /v1/stream (NDJSON), backpressure-aware
  # Eval harness is first-class and OSS (this is GeomTok-Eval):
  from geomtok.eval import GeomTokEval
  ev = GeomTokEval(tokenize_fn=tok.encode, detokenize_fn=tok.decode)
  ev.eval_scene("home", svg); print(ev.summary())            # attr_mean_err, count_acc, render_ssim, compression_vs_baseline
  Ergonomics: pinned tokenizer_version is a constructor arg (default = latest stable, warns on float); HuggingFace-style geomtok.Tokenizer.from_pretrained('geomtok-1.0.0'); typed dataclasses; numpy-friendly (encode_batch returns ragged list or padded np.ndarray via to_numpy=True); deterministic — same input+version always same ids (golden-file tested). Framework adapters: geomtok.torch.collate for padding/attention-mask, optional torch extra.

JAVASCRIPT/TS (npm i @geomtok/sdk) — isomorphic (Node + browser + edge/Workers):
  import { Tokenizer } from "@geomtok/sdk";
  const tok = new Tokenizer({ level: "L1", canvasSize: 300 });        // in-process WASM build of the core (no key needed)
  const ids = tok.encode(svgString);                                  // number[]
  const svg = tok.decode(ids);
  const hosted = new Tokenizer({ apiKey: "gk_live_...", baseUrl: "https://api.geomtok.dev" });
  const out = await hosted.encodeBatch([svg1, svg2]);                 // POST /v1/batch
  for await (const r of hosted.stream(svgAsyncIter)) { ... }          // NDJSON stream via fetch ReadableStream
  Ergonomics: full TS types generated from the OpenAPI spec; tree-shakeable; the WASM core ships the frozen vocab so browser-side encode is offline + deterministic and byte-identical to Python (cross-impl golden vectors in CI); zero-dep fetch client; ESM + CJS.

Shared SDK contract: identical method names across langs; tokenizer_version + vocab_id surfaced on every result; idempotency-key header auto-set on writes; exponential backoff + 429 Retry-After respected; errors are typed (GeomTokParseError, GeomTokVersionMismatch, RateLimitError). Cross-language determinism is a guaranteed, CI-enforced invariant — the same SVG yields identical token_ids in Python, JS-WASM, and the hosted server for a given tokenizer_version.
architecture:
Stateless, CPU-bound, deterministic microservice — the workload is pure function (svg, version, config) -> token_ids with no I/O dependency, which dictates a simple, aggressively-cacheable, horizontally-scaled design.

REQUEST PATH:
  Client/SDK -> API gateway/L7 LB (TLS, auth, rate-limit, request size cap 256KB single / 32MB batch)
             -> Tokenizer worker pool (stateless replicas, the OSS reference server packaged as a container)
             -> [async only] queue (SQS/Cloud Tasks) -> batch-job workers -> object store (R2/S3) sink + webhook.
  No database in the hot path. The only persistent state is auth/quota (Postgres or a managed KV) and object storage for async job artifacts — both off the synchronous tokenize/detokenize path.

WORKER INTERNALS:
  - Each replica is single-purpose: a thin HTTP server (FastAPI/uvicorn or a Rust/Go shim calling the core) wrapping the geomtok library. On boot it loads the frozen vocab tables + parser for every active tokenizer_version into resident memory (sub-100MB; no model weights — generation is excluded from v1.0).
  - CPU-pinned worker processes = N_cores; libsvg parsing + ARCS quantization are vectorized over batch items. Tokenization is O(path-commands), single-digit-ms per icon.
  - Multi-version: a replica can serve all active tokenizer_versions concurrently (each version = an immutable vocab+config bundle, content-addressed by sha256). Decode tables are looked up by the version on the request, never global mutable state.
  - Grammar/FSA-constrained decode path (GrammarMask) guarantees /v1/detokenize emits structurally-valid SVG even for adversarial/model-generated token streams.

CACHING:
  - Deterministic => cache key = hash(tokenizer_version + level + config + svg_bytes). A shared read-through cache (Redis/edge KV) short-circuits repeat tokenizations (icon libraries have heavy duplication). Cache-Control + strong ETag on responses; CDN-cacheable because output is a pure function of input.

SCALING & DEPLOYMENT:
  - Stateless replicas behind HPA/KEDA: scale on CPU utilization + p99 latency + queue depth. Because there is no warmup model load beyond vocab tables, cold start is seconds; scale-to-floor (not zero) to keep p99 tight, burst on demand.
  - Region-local pools; anycast/edge termination. Optional edge-WASM deployment of the core on Cloudflare Workers for ultra-low-latency single-icon tokenize at the edge (the same WASM the JS SDK uses).
  - Async batch jobs run on a separate, cheaper autoscaled worker class (spot/preemptible OK — deterministic + idempotent so re-runs are safe), isolated from the latency-sensitive sync pool.

ISOLATION:
  - The tokenizer touches no tenant data store, holds no per-tenant state, and forks no subprocess on tenant input -> the multi-tenant blast radius is one request. Per-tenant quotas/rate-limits enforced at the gateway; async job buckets are tenant-scoped with scoped credentials. Strict input bounds (size, element count, recursion depth on nested <g>/transform) prevent resource-exhaustion across tenants.

OSS REFERENCE SERVER: the exact container used in production is published Apache-2.0 (Dockerfile + Helm chart), so a customer can self-host the identical service; the hosted tier adds the surrounding control plane, not a forked core.
nonfunctional: Latency (sync single tokenize/detokenize, in-region, warm): p50 <= 8ms, p95 <= 25ms, p99 <= 60ms server-side compute (excludes network); the operation is single-digit-ms CPU per typical icon. /v1/eval per-scene adds render-SSIM cost (rasterization): p50 ~40ms/scene.

Throughput: a single 8-vCPU replica sustains ~3-6k single-icon tokenizations/sec (O(path-commands), no I/O); batch endpoint amortizes HTTP overhead for 10x effective items/sec. Linear horizontal scaling — capacity is a pure function of core count.

DETERMINISM (hard invariant): for a fixed (tokenizer_version, vocab_id, level, config), the same SVG bytes MUST yield byte-identical token_ids on every replica, every region, and across Python / JS-WASM / hosted implementations. Enforced by content-addressed frozen vocab bundles (sha256), golden-vector CI across all three impls, and no nondeterministic ops (no float reduction order dependence; fixed-point scalar coord codec, 0.04px). No silent retraining — a vocab/behavior change = a new tokenizer_version, never an in-place mutation.

VERSIONING & COMPAT: tokenizer_version is explicit, pinnable, and immutable; default points to latest stable but every response echoes the resolved version so clients can detect drift. Deprecation policy: >=12 months overlap, sunset dates published via /v1/versions, version-mismatch on decode is a typed 409 error (you cannot decode tokens with the wrong vocab).

FIDELITY GUARANTEES (published SLO, backed by measured numbers): 100% parse + round-trip on real-world icon corpus; coordinate fidelity 1.78px mean / 3.37px max on a 300px canvas; render SSIM 0.929; 3.54x token compression vs a matched domain-trained text tokenizer at 5,561 vocab. These are contractual quality targets surfaced via /v1/eval, not marketing claims.

MULTI-TENANT ISOLATION: no shared mutable per-tenant state in the hot path; per-tenant API keys, rate limits, and quotas at the gateway; per-tenant scoped object-store buckets for async jobs; strict input bounds (256KB/doc, 1000 items/batch, 32MB/batch payload, bounded <g>/transform nesting depth, parse-time budget) to cap any one tenant's resource use. Tenant input is never executed — SVG is parsed as data, scripts/foreignObject/external refs are stripped, never fetched.
AVAILABILITY: 99.9% on the synchronous tier (stateless replicas + multi-AZ + health-gated rollout make this cheap to hit); async batch tier 99.5% with at-least-once + idempotent processing.

RATE LIMITING: token-bucket per API key — e.g. free 60 req/min + 5k items/day; pro tier higher; 429 with Retry-After + X-RateLimit-* headers; batch items counted toward quota, not HTTP calls, so batching is encouraged not penalized.

SECURITY/COMPLIANCE: TLS 1.2+; API-key auth with scoped keys (tokenize-only vs eval vs job-submit); no tenant SVG retained beyond request lifecycle on the sync path (async job inputs/outputs live only in tenant-scoped buckets the tenant controls); SOC2-track audit logging on control-plane actions; input is sandboxed-by-construction (no eval of SVG, no network fetch of external entities).

OBSERVABILITY: per-request tokenizer_version + vocab_id + n_tokens + compression_ratio in structured logs and as response headers; RED metrics + latency histograms per endpoint/version; cache-hit ratio; cost-per-1k-tokens dashboards per tenant.
oss_vs_hosted_split:
OSS (Apache-2.0, free, self-hostable — the moat is the research, not withheld code):
  - geomtok core library (Python pip + @geomtok/sdk npm/WASM): full tokenize/detokenize, all levels L1/L2/L3, the scalar fixed-point coord codec, ARCS quantization, transform flattening + viewBox normalization, FSA grammar-constrained decode. In-process, no key, no network.
  - GeomTok-Eval: the entire render-based, game-resistant intrinsic evaluation protocol (eval_scene/summary, attr-error, count-accuracy, render-SSIM, token-economy vs baseline). This is the unique IP and it ships fully open — credibility and adoption depend on it being inspectable and reproducible. Researchers and vendors can evaluate ANY tokenizer (incl. competitors) through it.
  - Reference server: the exact production container, Dockerfile, Helm chart, OpenAPI spec, golden test vectors. A customer can stand up the identical stateless service themselves.
  - Frozen vocab bundles + version manifests are public and content-addressed, so self-hosted and hosted produce byte-identical tokens (no lock-in on the data format).

HOSTED / PAID (managed convenience + scale + governance around the same OSS core — NOT a forked or crippled engine):
  - Managed multi-region autoscaled API at api.geomtok.dev with the latency SLOs (p99 <= 60ms), 99.9% uptime, and burst capacity — customers pay to not run the CPU fleet, autoscaler, and cache themselves.
  - Control plane: API-key issuance + scoping, per-tenant rate limits/quotas, usage metering & billing, dashboards (tokens, compression, cost), audit logs.
  - Async large-corpus batch-job service (/v1/batch/jobs): queue, R2/S3 sink, webhooks, spot-worker fleet for million-icon backfills — operationally heavy, hence hosted.
  - Shared read-through cache + edge-WASM tokenization for sub-10ms global single-icon calls.
  - Managed eval-as-a-service: run GeomTok-Eval against your library/model on our compute with stored, shareable result reports.
  - Enterprise: version-pinning/LTS guarantees, SSO/SAML, VPC/private-link, SLA, support + consulting (the explicit revenue line).

LINE IN ONE SENTENCE: every byte of the tokenizer and the eval protocol is open and self-hostable; you pay only for managed operation at scale, the control plane, and async/enterprise services — never for the algorithm itself.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF v1.0 (later phase): the generation model (currently toy-scale 2.5M params, CPU, monochrome path icons) is NOT in the v1.0 product surface. /v1/generate, model hosting, and fine-tuning are deferred until large-data training investment lands. v1.0 is tokenizer + eval only — both production-ready now; generation ships later on top of the same token substrate (the F5 finding that geometric tokens are the best downstream substrate is the strategic reason to own the tokenizer layer first).
